guideTitle: 6 Best Hose Reel Carts Under $75 in 2026
metaTitle: 6 Best Hose Reel Carts Under $75 in 2026
metaDescription: Six budget hose reel carts and reels compared on rated hose length, steel versus resin, assembly and handle comfort, with notes on what spending more adds.
introParagraphs: At this budget, a hose reel cart is a trade between reach, materials and convenience. You can find carts rated for 300 feet, carts that arrive fully assembled, and compact reels that fit a balcony. What you rarely get is all three together, so the useful question is which compromise suits your yard.

This lineup covers six options. The Poakkus is rated for 300 feet of 5/8 inch hose on four 10 inch wheels, the GrillTown Hosemobile and a generic 175 foot cart arrive assembled, the VEVOR holds 175 feet in powder-coated steel, the Yestar cart holds 75 to 150 feet with an adjustable handrail, and the small Yestar reel holds 65 to 100 feet and hangs on a wall or carries by hand. We frame value tradeoffs throughout without quoting prices.

We evaluated each one based on product specs and buyer feedback, concentrating on rated length, frame material, fittings, assembly and winding comfort. Ratings assume a standard hose, and a thicker one lowers real capacity, so read every figure as a ceiling rather than a promise.

products.name: Poakkus 300 ft 4-Wheel Hose Reel Cart
products.description:
The Poakkus gives you the longest reach in this budget range: 300 feet of 5/8 inch hose on a four-wheel steel frame, with the hose not included. The listing describes a steel frame with a weather-resistant powder coating and brass fittings that help reduce leaks and corrosion. Four 10 inch PU wheels and a low center of gravity let the cart stay stable even when fully loaded.

An ergonomic non-slip crank handle makes winding quicker, and a built-in storage basket holds nozzles, sprinklers, and gloves. The tradeoff is size, because a 300 foot cart is large and heavy when full and hard to tuck into a small shed. It is also more cart than a small suburban lot needs, so the extra reach is wasted if your longest run is 100 feet. It suits large lawns, gardens, and farm-style properties.

For ownership, expect some assembly and plan a permanent storage spot, since this is not a cart you lift into a trunk. The steel coating needs to stay intact, so avoid leaving it in standing water. Compared with the VEVOR 175 foot cart, it holds 125 feet more and rolls on four wheels instead of two. Compared with the GrillTown Hosemobile, it is sturdier and far larger but needs assembling.
products.bestFor: Large yards where reach matters and a stable four-wheel stance is welcome.
pros: Four 10 inch wheels give a stable stance
cons: Large and heavy when fully loaded
Needs assembly and a big storage spot

products.name: VEVOR 175 ft Hose Reel Cart
products.description:
The VEVOR 175 foot cart holds up to 175 feet of 5/8 inch hose, with the hose not included. The structure is sturdy powder-coated steel with a weather-resistant coating and brass fittings, which the listing says resist rust and leakage. Two solid PVC wheels and a low center of gravity are meant to keep it from tipping on rough ground.

A non-slip handle makes winding easy, and the listing frames the cart as a cure for coming up short on hose length. Solid PVC wheels never go flat, which suits rough ground, though they give a firmer ride than pneumatic tires. The tradeoff is that two wheels mean the cart tilts back when you move it, so the handler carries some weight. A chipped coating can rust, so keep the finish intact.

For ownership, assembly is the main chore, and the brass fittings are a quiet advantage because the connection point is where most reels leak. Compared with the generic 175 foot cart, it adds brass and steel but needs tools. Compared with the Yestar cart at 75 to 150 feet, it holds more hose. Compared with the Poakkus at 300 feet, it is easier to store and push on two wheels but offers far less reach.
products.bestFor: Medium yards that want a sturdy steel cart with brass fittings without the bulk of 300 feet.
pros: Brass fittings resist leaks and rust
Solid PVC wheels never go flat
cons: Two wheels tilt back when moved
Steel can rust if the coating chips
Shorter reach than the Poakkus at 300 ft

products.name: 175 ft Portable Hose Reel Cart With 7 Inch Wheels
products.description:
This generic cart holds 175 feet of standard 5/8 inch hose and arrives fully assembled, so you simply attach your hose and start winding. Its 7 inch oversized wheels are described as giving better traction on grass, gravel or dirt. The body is weather-resistant resin that the listing says resists cracking and fading, and it measures 31.5 by 20.25 by 24.25 inches.

A handle hook with a leader hose holds the hose end in place so it does not unravel after winding, and a small compartment holds gloves, connectors, and nozzles. The ready-to-use setup is the main value at this tier, since assembly time is a hidden cost of cheap carts. The tradeoff is limited documentation, because the listing gives no weight limit, warranty, or fitting material. Resin is also less robust than steel under heavy load.

For ownership, the no-tools setup is a relief, and the bigger footprint means you need a reasonable shed space. Compared with the GrillTown Hosemobile, it adds a stated wheel size and a storage compartment. Compared with the VEVOR, it is easier to start but lacks the brass fittings and steel frame. It suits buyers who dislike assembly and want a light cart for a typical lawn.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a cart that works out of the box.
pros: 7 inch wheels for grass and gravel
Handle hook and small parts compartment
cons: No weight limit or warranty listed
Resin is less robust than steel

products.name: GrillTown Hosemobile 175 ft Hose Reel Cart
products.description:
The Hosemobile holds 175 feet of 5/8 inch hose, arrives fully assembled and uses sturdy resin construction. The listing mentions an Easylink system that ensures a watertight connection between the reel and your hoses. Dimensions are 22 inches wide, 45 inches high, and 22.8 inches long, so it is a tall, upright cart.

Resin keeps the weight down and will not rust, which helps both lifting and upkeep. Fully assembled means no tools and no lost screws, so it is a low-effort option for casual use. The tradeoff is limited documentation, because the listing gives no wheel size, handle details, or finish information. Resin is also less robust than steel under heavy load or in cold weather.

For ownership, expect basic function and a tall profile that tucks into a corner of the garage more easily than a wide cart. Compared with the generic 175 foot cart, it states a watertight connection system but fewer wheel details. Compared with the Poakkus, it is much lighter and holds 125 feet less. It suits buyers who want a simple, light cart that is ready on day one.
products.bestFor: Casual users who want a light, no-assembly cart.
cons: Wheel and handle details not listed

products.name: Yestar Hose Reel Cart With Adjustable Handrail
specs: Holds 75 to 150 ft of 5/8 inch hose
products.description:
The Yestar cart holds 75 to 150 feet of 5/8 inch hose and features an adjustable handrail that you set to your height with a carabiner design. The reel frame is weather-resistant powder-coated metal with an aluminum tube support and plastic fittings. A non-slip handle helps roll the hose up without kinks.

An adjustable handrail is uncommon at this tier and helps shorter and taller users share one cart. The listing says assembly takes about 10 minutes and points to an installation video, and the box includes a manual and spare accessories. The tradeoff is plastic fittings, which are less leak-resistant than the brass on the Poakkus and VEVOR. The wide 75 to 150 foot range also means real capacity depends heavily on hose thickness.

For ownership, plan to unwind from a flat spot and check the fittings now and then for drips. Compared with the small Yestar reel, it is a rolling cart with a higher ceiling. Compared with the VEVOR at 175 feet, it holds less but adds the adjustable handrail. It suits small to mid-size yards where several people use the same cart.
products.bestFor: Small to mid-size yards shared by users of different heights.
cons: Plastic fittings can leak sooner than brass
Capacity range is wide and hose dependent
Aluminum support is lighter duty than steel

products.name: Yestar Portable Hose Reel Holds 65 to 100 ft
products.description:
The small Yestar reel is a compact plastic unit that can be mounted on a wall or carried by hand. It holds 65 to 100 feet of 5/8 inch hose, or 85 to 120 feet of 1/2 inch hose. The listing says installation needs no tools and comes with a manual and installation video.

Because it is light, it is the easiest pick here to lift and the easiest to put away. The tradeoff is that it has no wheels, so you carry it rather than roll it, and plastic is less tough than metal under heavy loads. A labor-saving handle speeds up winding. It suits patios, balconies, and small gardens where a big cart would be overkill.

For ownership, mounting it to a wall saves floor space and keeps the hose off the ground, which also protects the hose from sun and foot traffic. Compared with the Yestar cart at 75 to 150 feet, it holds less and lacks wheels. Compared with the Poakkus at 300 feet, it is a different tool entirely, with a fraction of the reach but a fraction of the storage footprint.
products.bestFor: Balconies, patios, and small gardens where space and weight matter most.
cons: No wheels, so you carry it
Plastic is less durable than metal
Capacity limited to about 100 ft of 5/8 inch

buyingCriteria.explanation: Ratings assume a standard 5/8 inch hose, and a thicker hose takes more drum space so you fit less. The Poakkus rates 300 feet, the VEVOR, GrillTown, and generic carts rate 175, the Yestar cart rates 75 to 150, and the small Yestar reel rates 65 to 100. Pick a cart rated at least 10 percent above your hose to avoid overfilling. Overfilling causes uneven winding and strain on the frame, and it is the most common reason a budget cart feels hard to crank.

Steel is stronger but heavier and can rust if the coating chips, while resin and plastic are light and rust-free but less robust under load. The Poakkus and VEVOR use powder-coated steel, the GrillTown and generic cart use resin, and the small Yestar uses plastic. For a lawn that sees daily use, steel is the safer bet. For a light-duty cart that moves around a lot, the resin picks at 175 feet are easier to live with.

The connection point is where most hose reels start dripping, so the fitting material matters more than it looks. The Poakkus and VEVOR list brass fittings, the GrillTown lists an Easylink watertight connection, and the Yestar cart uses plastic fittings. Brass resists corrosion and thread wear for years of seasonal use. If you plan to leave the hose pressurized, favor brass and check the washer each spring.

Four wheels stand on their own while two wheels tilt and put weight on your arms. The Poakkus uses four 10 inch PU wheels, the VEVOR uses two solid PVC wheels, and the generic 175 foot cart has 7 inch wheels. Larger wheels roll over roots and soft turf, and solid wheels never go flat. Check wheel details for uneven yards, since a small wheel on soft ground sinks.

Cheap carts often hide assembly time. The GrillTown and the generic 175 foot cart arrive fully assembled, while the Poakkus, VEVOR, and Yestar cart need assembly, and the Yestar maker quotes about 10 minutes. If you are not handy, fully assembled carts avoid frustration. Otherwise budget an hour for the heavier steel carts and keep the screws in a tray.

Winding is the most tiring part of using a hose reel. The Poakkus has an ergonomic non-slip crank, the Yestar cart has an adjustable handrail on a carabiner, and the VEVOR has a non-slip handle. A comfortable grip matters even more with 175 feet or more of hose in the drum. Wind evenly and keep a hand on the hose near the cart to prevent tangles.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We used stated ratings. The Poakkus leads at 300 feet, the VEVOR, GrillTown, and generic carts follow at 175 feet, and the Yestar cart and small reel rate lower. All assume a standard hose, so we treated each figure as a ceiling.

howWeEvaluated.title: Build and fittings
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared frame materials and connection points. The Poakkus and VEVOR use powder-coated steel with brass fittings, the GrillTown and generic cart use resin, and the Yestar models use powder-coated metal with plastic fittings or plain plastic. Listings that skipped fitting details were rated cautiously.

howWeEvaluated.title: Setup
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked assembly state. The GrillTown and generic 175 foot cart arrive fully assembled, the Yestar cart assembles in about 10 minutes, and the steel carts take longer. The small Yestar reel installs without tools.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mobility
howWeEvaluated.description: Wheel details were weighed. The Poakkus has four 10 inch PU wheels, the VEVOR has two solid PVC wheels, and the generic cart has 7 inch wheels. The small Yestar reel has no wheels at all.

howWeEvaluated.title: Comfort and value
howWeEvaluated.description: Handles and adjustability mattered. The Yestar cart's adjustable handrail and the Poakkus crank stand out, and the Poakkus leads on reach while the VEVOR leads on steel and brass at a mid-size capacity. We noted missing details as gaps, not guesses.

faq.q: Is a cheap hose reel cart worth it?
faq.a: Yes for basic needs. The Poakkus offers 300 feet with brass fittings and the VEVOR offers powder-coated steel with brass fittings. Expect fewer premium touches such as documented hose guides or pneumatic tires. Match the cart to your yard size and it will serve for many seasons.

faq.q: How much hose will it hold?
faq.a: Ratings assume 5/8 inch hose. The Poakkus rates 300 feet, the VEVOR, GrillTown, and generic carts rate 175, and the Yestar cart rates 75 to 150. Thicker hose lowers real length, so a heavy rubber hose may fill the drum well short of the rating.

faq.q: Does the hose come with it?
faq.a: Generally not. The Poakkus and VEVOR state hose is not included, and the other listings sell only the cart. Buy a hose rated for the cart and keep a short leader hose in mind for the connection.

faq.q: Is resin as good as steel?
faq.a: Resin is lighter and will not rust, but it is less robust under heavy loads and in the cold. Steel lasts longer under load but needs its coating kept intact. Choose by how much you value light weight versus durability.

Wind evenly and avoid overfilling beyond the rated length. Drain the hose before winding and keep it taut as it enters the drum. The Yestar cart notes that its non-slip handle helps roll the hose up without kinks.

They matter because the connection point is where leaks start. The Poakkus and VEVOR list brass fittings, which resist corrosion and wear better than plastic. If you leave the hose pressurized between uses, brass is worth prioritizing.

Spend more for documented hose guides, pneumatic tires, and a longer warranty. If your cart leaks, kinks, or sinks in soft ground, those upgrades matter. Otherwise a simple cart like the VEVOR 175 footer covers most medium yards.
